S014-01.notes: Laying out all explanations without picking one = noncommittal. 'Ambivalent' (mixed feelings) is the intended near-miss trap; 'indifferent' implies lack of care, contradicted by 'meticulously'; 'partisan' is the opposite.

flags: minor: key word 'recondite' is high-difficulty vocabulary, but the three distractors are clearly eliminable (derivative/accessible contradict the context, prolific is irrelevant), so elimination rescues many students
S014-02.notes: Dense allusions to obscure texts few could follow = recondite (obscure, abstruse).

S014-03.notes: Rural gap 73-64=9 vs urban 75-72=3; only A compares the gaps.

S014-04.notes: Bees remember and return to caffeinated flowers -> repeat visits aid pollination.

flags: Ambiguous key risk: in 'one of the few marine biologists who ___ observed', the antecedent of 'who' is the plural 'biologists' (she is one of the biologists who have observed...), so traditional/prescriptive grammar requires 'have' (A). If the key is 'has' (B), it is defensible only under informal notional agreement and is contestable; either way both A and B have supporters, so the item does not have exactly one uncontroversially correct answer. Recommend rewriting (e.g., 'Dr. Osei, a marine biologist, ___ observed' or remove 'one of the few').
S014-05.notes: Subject-verb agreement in relative clause after 'one of the ... who'; antecedent is plural 'biologists' -> 'have'. Most quick solvers pick 'has' by attaching to 'one'/'Dr. Osei'.

S014-06.notes: No punctuation between verb 'argued' and its 'that' clause object, nor after 'that' before the subject.

S014-07.notes: Infants' sensitive period for language parallels songbirds' -> Similarly.
